DESIGN REMOTE MICROGRIDS WITH ENHANCED RESILIENCE: ANALYSIS, PROTOTYPING, AND MODULARIZATION.  

THE OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP, PROTOTYPE AND DEMONSTRATE MODULAR MICROGRID SYSTEMS WITH STANDARDIZED FUNCTIONALITIES AND ADVANCED BLACK START CONTROL.  THESE MICROGRIDS ARE INTENDED TO FORTIFY THE TRIBE'S RESILIENCE AGAINST EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS.

DYNAMIC MODULAR MICROGRIDS (DYM-MGS): REAL-TIME AND PACKETIZED MICROGRID IMPLEMENTATION. THE TEAM PROPOSES TO DEVELOP A DYNAMIC AND MODULAR MICROGRID (DYM-MG) SOLUTION WITH FEATURES AND CHARACTERISTICS OF QUANTIFIABLE RESILIENCE ENHANCEMENT, INHERENT TRANSIENT STABILITY, AND MULTI-STAGE OPTIMAL OPERATION IN BOTH “BLUE-SKY” AND “BLACK-SKY” CONDITIONS.

COORDINATED DEVELOPMENT OF STANDARDIZED MODULAR MICROGRID CONTROL SYSTEMS FOR REMOTE ALASKAN COMMUNITIES.

THE PROJECT ADVANCES STANDARDIZED, MODULAR MICRO-GRID CONTROL DESIGNS, WHILE EXPANDING COLLABORATIVE DEVELOPMENT METHODS TO ALLOW REMOTE COMMUNITIES TO PLAY A CENTRAL ROLE IN THE DESIGN AND MANAGEMENT OF THEIR OWN MICRO-GRID CONTROL SYSTEMS. REMOTE COMMUNITIES WILL BE ENGAGED AND PROVIDED TOOLS TO COLLECT DATA ABOUT THEIR LOCAL ENERGY SYSTEM AND ENERGY NEEDS IN A MANNER THAT STANDARDIZES THE DATA, ALLOWING THE DATA TO BE USED IN MODEL-BASED SIMULATIONS MIMICKING A VARIETY OF SYSTEM-TYPES AND CHARACTERISTICS. THE OUTCOMES WILL ALLOW COMMUNITIES TO MOVE AWAY FROM THE VERY HIGH COST THAT MICROGRID DEVELOPERS OFFERS ALONG WITH THE REQUIREMENTS TO COMMIT TO LONG-TERM CONTRACTS WITH EXTERNALLY PROVIDED CONTROL PLATFORMS.
